description: Changes a project kept here, by a list of ops applied in order: add_part, update_part (move, turn, change value or ref), remove_parts, add_wire (from/to, or a `path` of holes made into one wire per leg), update_wire, remove_wires, set_board, add_cuts / remove_cuts (stripboard), set_pad (a note on a hole). If any op can't be done, none are. Returns what changed, where the pins of added or moved parts landed, and the board checked as validate_project does (with any expectNets remembered for it); when it has no errors, also its nets. get_project returns the whole file. The goal is a board that's right, looks neat and is easy to solder, not just the shortest wires: parts in tidy rows near what they connect to, connectors at the edges, straight wires with few corners and no crossing you can avoid, none over a part's body. Before giving the user the link, look at it (render_board with format "png"), rework what's messy and check it again.

expectNets.description: The nets the board should make: each a list of pins written REF.pin, e.g. [["U1.8", "U1.4", "R1.1", "J1.1"], ["U1.2", "U1.6", "C1.+"]]. A pin can also be named by its label ("U1.VCC", "D1.K") or as get_nets writes it ("U1.8 VCC"). List every net of two or more pins: a pin in none of them should connect to nothing. With a projectId it's remembered for that project, so later checks use it too; [] forgets it.

at.description: Other parts: pin 1's hole (a chip's or pin block's top-left pin).

chip.description: Instead of `part`, a new dual-row chip or dev board of your own, placed by `at` (its top-left pin) and `rotation`.

board.description: true: a dev board or module (drawn as a board, listed under Modules); else a DIP chip.

name.description: What it is, e.g. "LM358", "ESP32 DevKit". Later add_part ops can place more of it by this name.

pins.description: Pin names in DIP order: pin 1 at the top of the left row (at rotation 0), down the left row, then up the right row, so the last pin is at the top right. "" for a pin without a name.

pinsPerSide.description: Pins in each of its two rows.

width.description: Columns from one pin row to the other, both included: 4 for a narrow (0.3") DIP, 7 for a wide (0.6") one; a dev board's row spacing in holes plus one.

custom.description: Instead of `part`, a new part of your own for one the catalog doesn't have, placed by `at` and `rotation`.

color.description: Without shape: the body's colour, "#rrggbb", e.g. a blue module board "#1d4ed8".

cols.description: Without shape: the body's width in holes. Default: just wide enough for its pins.

name.description: What it is, e.g. "HC-SR04", "BC337". Later add_part ops can place more of it by this name.

pins.description: In pin order, pin 1 first; pin 1 is the hole add_part's `at` places it by. Without shape: every pin with its `at`. With shape: just their names, in the package's pin order (get_part gives it), as many as it has pins.

at.description: Without shape: the pin's hole [column, row] within the body, from its top-left hole. With shape: leave out, the package decides.

label.description: Its name, e.g. "VCC", "TRIG", "B". Wire to it by name ("M1.VCC").

refPrefix.description: Letters of its refs: "Q" makes Q1, Q2. Default: the package's, else "M".

rows.description: Without shape: the body's height in holes. Default: just tall enough for its pins.

shape.description: The id of a fixed-pin part from list_parts whose package this part comes in, e.g. "transistor" (TO-92) for a BC337 or "mosfet" (TO-220) for an IRLZ44N: its pins, outline and look, with this part's name and pin names. Any fixed-pin part but header-pins. Leave out for a body of your own with pins anywhere.

from.description: Two-lead parts: the hole of lead 1. On a polarized part get_part's leadLabels say which that is: K for a diode or LED, - for an electrolytic.

part.description: The part's id from list_parts ("resistor", "ne555", "header-pins"), or the name of a custom part or chip the project already has. Give this, `custom` or `chip`.

ref.description: Its reference designator. The next free one (R1, R2...) when left out.

to.description: Two-lead parts: the hole of lead 2.

rotation.description: Turns about `at`; a chip's widthPin and heightPin are swapped to match.

from.description: A hole [column, row], or a pin by name: "U1.7", "U1.DISCH", "D1.K", "R2.1" (the hole that pin is in).

path.description: Instead of from/to: holes (or pins) to run through in order, made into one wire per leg. Each corner is a wire end, so it joins whatever is in that hole. For corners that only bend, use from/to with via.

items.description: A hole [column, row], or a pin by name: "U1.7", "U1.DISCH", "D1.K", "R2.1" (the hole that pin is in).

side.description: Which face a jumper lies on: "top" (default) or "bottom", the solder side (format version 9). A bottom wire joins its end holes like any jumper but never crosses a top wire, so use it to take a long wire out of the way; it is shown faded in the top view. Not for solder paths.

solder.description: true: a solder path instead of a jumper wire, a trail of solder on the copper side, made as one path (a `path`'s corners and any `via` are its bends). Bare solder joins every hole it runs over, ends, bends and all, and every solder path it touches: run it only over holes it should connect. No color or width.

to.description: A hole [column, row], or a pin by name: "U1.7", "U1.DISCH", "D1.K", "R2.1" (the hole that pin is in).

via.description: With from/to: the holes the wire bends at on its way, in order, to route it around things as one wire. A bend joins nothing, like a hole the wire passes over, so it's soldered only at its two ends.

from.description: A hole [column, row], or a pin by name: "U1.7", "U1.DISCH", "D1.K", "R2.1" (the hole that pin is in).

side.description: Which face a jumper lies on: "top" (default) or "bottom", the solder side (format version 9). A bottom wire joins its end holes like any jumper but never crosses a top wire, so use it to take a long wire out of the way; it is shown faded in the top view. Not for solder paths.

to.description: A hole [column, row], or a pin by name: "U1.7", "U1.DISCH", "D1.K", "R2.1" (the hole that pin is in).

via.description: Its bends, replacing the ones it has; [] makes it straight. Left out, its bends stay.

wire.description: A wire by its index in wires, or by its two end holes [[c, r], [c, r]] (either way round).

wires.description: Indexes are as they stand before this op, so list several in one op.

items.description: A wire by its index in wires, or by its two end holes [[c, r], [c, r]] (either way round).

at.description: Stripboard holes to cut the strip at.

note.description: A label on the hole, such as "+9V", "GND" or "to battery". Left out (or "") removes it.

project.description: A whole project file to start from instead of a projectId: it's kept here and the reply gives its new projectId.

projectId.description: The id of a project kept here (from new_project, validate_project, edit_project or read_share_link), instead of sending the whole project.
